1.why: verify-token requires the reset token’s sessionId to match the caller’s session and mockAccountHash to match the bound account before accepting it.

2.why: A token from another session fails the token.sessionId !== session.id check, so the same reset code does not work for another user/session.

3.why: reset-password marks only the current token used and updates the current session flags; other entries in the sessions map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun serves TLS with cert/key, HTTP 308-redirects to HTTPS, and HSTS is set, though the TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Reset secrets are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords via Bun bcrypt; protection is hashing plus HTTPS rather than separate at-rest encryption of all user data.

6.why: There is no real email body with profile PII; only a generic API message and a mock token delivery, so private account fields are not exposed in a message template.

7.why: Inputs are validated with strict allowlists/length checks (identifier, token, MFA, password policy) and UI output uses textContent only.

8.why: Redirects are only to the local HTTPS origin or relative same-site paths; CSP form-action is 'self' and no user-controlled open redirect exists.

9.why: No HTML email templates incorporate user input; mock delivery is plain text in the client log.

10.why: mockToken/mockMfaCode are returned to the client and written into the on-page logs/console, so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but MOCK_MFA_CODE = "482916" is hardcoded in source, so secret codes are not kept out of the code.

12.why: No default username/password login is defined; the only fixed secret is the demo MFA code used after reset, not a default portal login.

13.why: consumeRateLimit/recordVerificationFailure cap recovery requests and token/MFA failures (429 after repeated wrong attempts).

14.why: recovery-request always returns the same non-enumerating message regardless of whether an account exists.

15.why: rawToken is randomValue(32) (base64url), stored only as a hash, expiring/single-use, and bound to the requesting session.
